title: Locality of KMS states for infinite fermionic lattice systems
abstract: We study how thermal equilibrium states of infinite fermionic lattices respond to perturbations of the Hamiltonian. Our main result concerns extensive perturbations of a chosen KMS state. We show that exponential decay of correlations and exponential local indistinguishability under the extensive perturbation yield stretched-exponential decay of correlations for the perturbed state. Neither the initial nor the perturbed state is required to be unique, allowing stability to be studied in the presence of phase coexistence. Our approach uses Quantum Belief Propagation (QBP), which we establish directly on the underlying $C^*$-algebra. Combining QBP with Lieb--Robinson bounds, we show implications between decay of correlations, the principle that local perturbations perturb locally, and local indistinguishability, closing the cycle for perturbations of the tracial state under the stated decay, support and uniformity assumptions. For extensive perturbations under uniform clustering conditions, we also obtain a differentiable path of local equilibrium expectations and bound their change linearly in the interaction norm of the perturbation.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes how thermal equilibrium states (KMS states) of infinite fermionic lattices change when the system Hamiltonian is perturbed. Using advanced tools like Quantum Belief Propagation and Lieb-Robinson bounds, the authors prove that strong initial locality properties lead to specific, quantifiable decay rates in the perturbed state. This advances the understanding of stability and locality in quantum many-body physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the stability of locality properties of thermal (KMS) states in infinite fermionic lattice systems when the Hamiltonian is subjected to perturbations.
main_result: It shows that under certain decay conditions, exponential decay of correlations and local indistinguishability for the initial state imply stretched-exponential decay for the perturbed state.
method: The authors employ Quantum Belief Propagation (QBP) formulated on the $C^*$-algebra, combined with Lieb-Robinson bounds, to establish rigorous mathematical implications between various notions of locality.
model_or_system: The system is an infinite fermionic lattice described by a $C^*$-algebra, with the study focusing on the $(	au,  eta)$-KMS state and its response to extensive perturbations $V$.
key_observables: Decay of correlations, Local Indistinguishability (LI), and the differentiability of local equilibrium expectations.
important_parameters: The decay rates (exponential vs. stretched-exponential), the interaction norm of the perturbation, and the temperature parameter $ eta$.
main_assumptions: The results rely on specific decay, support, and uniformity assumptions regarding the perturbations and the underlying state structure.
paper_structure: The paper builds mathematically by first establishing the $C^*$-dynamical system framework, then applying QBP to characterize perturbed KMS states, and finally using Lieb-Robinson bounds to derive the decay estimates for locality.
why_interesting: The rigorous connection between correlation decay, local perturbations, and local indistinguishability provides powerful tools for understanding how local physics dictates global thermal properties in interacting quantum many-body systems.
